summary: After two subjective days of successful simulation testing, [[character:bob-replicant]] learns that only two candidates remain after one suffered a psychotic break and [[character:minister-travis]] rejected another, who appears to have been purged. [[character:dr-landers]] reveals that the winner will control a self-replicating interstellar probe. Newly eager to reach the stars, Bob applies himself to studying project documents and coordinating autonomous [[technology:roamers]] through a repair exercise.

introducing.name: Von Neumann probe
introducing.description: A self-replicating spacecraft designed to travel between star systems and construct new copies of itself along the way.

introducing.name: nanites
introducing.description: Tiny, single-purpose devices used for work below ROAMer scale; their flexibility is limited.

updates.current_state: Training as one of two remaining candidates to control a [[technology:von-neumann-probe]].

updates.description: The Free American Independent Theocratic Hegemony, a theocratic U.S. government that makes criticism a felony and permits the deactivation of machine persons for it. It restricts information by default and is split into factions, some regarding AI and replicants as abominations or rejecting all technology since steam power. It finances the replicant project and owns [[character:bob-replicant]].

An interface that offloads tasks for replicants while retaining their human limits on multitasking. Its name expands to General Unit Primary Peripheral Interface, and its logs retain monitoring-interface and script activity.

Remote observation and manipulation devices directed through [[technology:guppi-interface|GUPPI]]. They come in varied sizes, can coordinate across scales, and need minimal supervision once their tasks, dependencies, and interruption conditions are defined. Without active intervention, they can work up to ten times faster.
